decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted shall not be carried out except in complete accordance with the details shown on the submitted plans, numbers:
PL-01; PL-02 Rev. P2
and shall thereafter be retained/maintained for as long as the development remains in existence.
REASON
To ensure the development complies with the provisions Hillingdon Local Plan Parts 1 (November 2012) and 2 (January 2020) and the London Plan (2021).

The use hereby permitted shall not take place other than between the hours of 1000 and 1900 on Mondays to Fridays and between 1100 and 1400 on Saturdays, and shall not take place at any time on Sundays or Bank Holidays.
REASON

To safeguard the living conditions of neighbouring occupiers from unacceptable noise, activity and disturbance, in accordance with Policy D14 of the London Plan (2021), Policy EM8 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 1, Strategic Policies (2012), and Policy DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2, Development Management Policies (2020).

The premises shall be used as a Women's Education and Recreation Institute and for no other purpose, including any other purpose within Class F1 of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987, as amended, or in any provision equivalent to that Class in any statutory instrument revoking and re-enacting that Order, with or without modification.
REASON

To safeguard the living conditions of neighbouring occupiers from unacceptable noise, activity and disturbance, in accordance with Policy D14 of the London Plan (2021), Policy EM8 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 1, Strategic Policies (2012), and Policy DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2, Development Management Policies (2020).

The use hereby permitted shall take place in accordance with the details of the Site Management Supervision Plan (Reference: 14AFILH-2073) (or those parts of the Plan capable of being implemented subject to other conditions herewith attached) dated 30.12.2025, Complaints Handling Policy & Procedure (Policy No: CHP/01) dated 15.10.2025, and Responses to Officer's Comments submitted on 05.06.2026. Those parts of the Plan capable of implementation shall continue to be implemented as long as any part of the premises is occupied for the use hereby permitted.
REASON

To ensure that the premises operate in a controlled and properly supervised manner and to safeguard the living conditions of neighbouring occupiers, parking conditions, the free flow of traffic and highway and pedestrian safety, in accordance with Policy D14 of the London Plan (2021), Policy EM8 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 1 (2012), and Policies DMHB 11, DMT 1 and DMT 2 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020).

The use hereby permitted shall be carried out and thereafter operated in accordance with the Travel Plan prepared by John Russell Transport Planning Ltd dated 29 December 2025 and the Parking Management Strategy prepared by John Russell Transport Planning Ltd dated 1 September 2026. Those parts of the Travel Plan capable of implementation shall continue to be implemented as long as any part of the premises is occupied for the use hereby permitted.
REASON

To promote sustainable travel, manage parking demand and vehicle movements, minimise overspill parking and safeguard the free flow of traffic and highway and pedestrian safety, in accordance with Policies T4, T5 and T6 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies DMT 1, DMT 2, DMT 5 and DMT 6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020).

The records of implementation and monitoring of the Travel Plan, including the results of the travel surveys, shall be made available to the Local Planning Authority on a regular basis, that basis being not less frequent than annually.
REASON

To enable the Local Planning Authority to monitor the effectiveness of the approved travel and parking management measures and ensure that the use does not result in unacceptable parking, congestion or highway-safety impacts, in accordance with Policies T4 and T6 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies DMT 1, DMT 2 and DMT 6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020).

The vehicle parking, access and manoeuvring arrangements shown on Drawing No. PL-02 Rev. P2 shall be retained and kept permanently available for the parking and manoeuvring of vehicles associated with the use hereby permitted. The parking arrangements shall be operated in accordance with the  Parking Management Strategy prepared by John Russell Transport Planning Ltd dated 1 September 2026. The parking and manoeuvring areas shall not be used for any other purpose.
REASON

To ensure that adequate parking and manoeuvring arrangements are retained, to minimise the potential for overspill parking and congestion, and to safeguard the free flow of traffic and highway and pedestrian safety, in accordance with Policies T4 and T6 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies DMT 1, DMT 2 and DMT 6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2, Development Management Policies (2020).

Within three months of the date of this permission, details of the existing or proposed secure and covered cycle-storage facilities shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include the location, design, capacity and means of access to the facilities.

Any additional or replacement facilities required by the approved details shall be provided within two months of the written approval of the details. The approved cycle-storage facilities shall thereafter be retained, maintained and kept available for users of the premises and shall not be used for any other purpose.
REASON

To encourage active and sustainable travel and reduce reliance on private motor vehicles, in accordance with Policy T5 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy DMT 5 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020).

Within three months of the date of this permission, details of the refuse and recycling storage arrangements shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include the location, capacity, design, screening and arrangements for collection of refuse and recyclable materials.

The approved facilities shall be provided within two months of the written approval of the details and shall thereafter be retained, maintained and used for the storage of refuse and recyclable materials associated with the use hereby permitted.
REASON

To ensure that refuse and recyclable materials are stored and collected in a satisfactory manner and to safeguard the character and appearance of the site and the living conditions of neighbouring occupiers, in accordance with Policies D3 and D6 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies DMHB 11 and DMHB 12 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020).

Within three months of the date of this permission, details of the existing and proposed hard and soft landscaping at the front of the premises shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include:
- means of enclosure;
- pedestrian access and circulation areas;
- hard-surfacing materials;
- existing planting to be retained;
- schedules of any proposed planting, including species, sizes, numbers and densities; and
- a timetable for implementation.

The approved landscaping works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved timetable. All hard landscaping shall thereafter be retained. Any tree, shrub or other planting that, within a period of five years from planting, dies, is removed, becomes seriously damaged or diseased shall be replaced in the next available planting season with planting of a similar size and species, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

No more than 30 persons, including staff, pupils and other visitors, shall be present within the application premises at any one time.

Reason: To control the intensity of the use and safeguard the living conditions of neighbouring occupiers, parking conditions, the free flow of traffic and highway and pedestrian safety, in accordance with Policy D14 of the London Plan (2021), Policy EM8 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 1 (2012), and Policies DMHB 11, DMT 1, DMT 2 and DMT 6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020).

The decision to GRANT planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to GRANT planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan (2021) and national guidance.

In dealing with the application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to work with the applicant in a positive and proactive way. We have made available detailed advice in the form of our statutory policies from Local Plan Part 1, Local Plan Part 2, Supplementary Planning Documents, Planning Briefs and other informal written guidance, as well as offering a full pre-application advice service, in order to ensure that the applicant has been given every opportunity to submit an application which is likely to be considered favourably.

The Equality Act 2010 seeks to protect people accessing goods, facilities and services from discrimination on the basis of a 'protected characteristic', which includes those with a disability. As part of the Act, service providers are obliged to improve access to and within the structure of their building, particularly in situations where reasonable adjustment can be incorporated with relative ease. The Act states that service providers should think ahead to take steps to address barriers that impede disabled people.
description: Variation of Conditions 2 (approved plans), 3 (hours of use), 5 (Site Management Supervision Plan), 6 (Travel Plan) and 8 (parking arrangements) of planning permission ref. APP/R5510/A/12/2177686, dated 18 December 2012, for 'Change of use from Guest House B&B to Class D1 Non-residential Institution for a Women's Education and Recreation Institute, involving formation of a staff car parking area to the rear (Retrospective application)', to permit additional evening and Saturday hours, substitute the approved plans and update the site management, travel and parking arrangements, together with the imposition of an additional condition limiting the maximum occupancy to 30 persons at any one time.
